A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

items.title: A tile clears at the market it is most attracted to: logistics cost over the centre's pull, not grid distance
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "Markets should be mildly dynamic, where each tile has a market attraction for each market, based on logistics distance to that market centre and also a modifier for that market centre which can come from either tech nodes or buildings." DESIGNED: MARKETS.md section Catchment is an attraction, not a distance; LOGISTICS.md section 3b (the off-road leg); GLOSSARY Market attraction. Today market_for_tile is nearest centre_tile by SQUARED GRID DISTANCE, column wrapped (market_clearing.cpp:165-284), cached in an unsaved raster rebuilt on market-set change - it cannot see a road, a tech or a building. New: attraction = traversal cost (LOGISTICS.md section 1) / centre pull, lowest wins, ties to the lowest market id; pull is a modifier_set multiplier, 1 by default. OFF-ROAD (Ben's call): a tile with no roaded edge costs the nearest roaded tile's network cost PLUS off-road-per-tile x the 4-cardinal step count to it (column wrapped), so every tile belongs to a market and far land drifts between markets as roads approach. Reach (section 3) is NOT changed - catchment and permission stay separate. CADENCE (Ben's call): recompute on change - a road laid or cut, a pull gained or lost, a market carved or folded - never on a clock, so it stays a pure function of standing state and is still never saved. A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability and haulage_measure --far-trade before and after; a re-bless is Ben's. Sequenced after BL-1340 (roads are edges), which changes what a roaded tile is. SAME-NATION BONUS (Ben, 2026-10-16): a tile owned by the same nation as the centre is 1.2x as attracted to it - a property of the (tile, centre) PAIR, not of the centre, so a centre pulls harder only on its own ground. Written into MARKETS.md. Measure how many tiles actually change hands at 1.2: the bonus is small against the cost spread, so report the count of tiles whose market flips because of it, per seed, and say so if it flips almost none.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the logistics visibility message); filed by Claude
items.title: Two unrelated Logistic Point systems are live at once, and the lens and marches read the retired one
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found mapping Ben's 2026-10-16 logistics message). THE ROOT CAUSE of what Ben saw in play. Two LP systems stand in the tree: (1) THE REAL ONE, BL-1309, src/world/logistic_points.*: a pool per NATION made only by inland hubs (120/tick), railway stations (150) and ports (120), scaled by each source's upkeep supply, with a bounded-Dijkstra reach field per (nation, network, body) that is full strength to lp_full_reach {6,10,12} then fades to zero over lp_fade_length {6,8,8}; consumed ONLY by production (lp_need = 10 x workforce run), granted pro-rata or by the nation's share rule, and spent as a labour multiplier so half the points means half the output. (2) THE LEGACY ONE, BL-596, active_lp_anchor_pools in logistics.cpp:1075: a flat 20/tick pool at every ANCHOR, where collect_anchor_tile_set (:31) seeds an anchor at EVERY population centre plus every port and hub - no falloff, no nation, no rail. Marching units still draw the legacy pools (economy_system.cpp:4210-4300, first-come in unit-id order). THE THROUGHPUT LENS READS ONLY THE LEGACY ONE. So Ben's reading that cities supply logistics is true of the system he can SEE and false of the one that runs the economy - the doc already ruled 'Cities make none' (2026-10-14). THE WORK: one system. Retire the legacy anchor pools, move the march draw onto the nation pool (the march is the priced consumer - LOGISTICS.md's 'Active lands first' and 'Armies claim first' need re-reading against a model where trade draws nothing at all), and point the lens at the real model (BL-1353). RECONCILED 2026-10-16: do NOT delete the passive-LP remains - Ben ruled the same day that a shipment draws points again (BL-1361), so market_lp_left (supply_system.cpp:1035, returns 0), market_component::trade_lp_spare (permanently 0, serialised at save v46, read by corp_ai) and corp_command rejected_no_lp are REVIVED by that item, not retired. Retire only the legacy ANCHOR pools and the march path that reads them.

items.title: The throughput lens: per-tile point numbers, the player's own nation only, no taglines, and roads recoloured in the pass that already redraws them
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "let's change the throughput lens, we can drop the '(active logistics points)' taglines, and give a number to each tile, so we can see exactly how many points we have. The lens should also be player facing, so we can see only the player's home nation's road network and points... instead let's recolour the roads to be a brighter white." TAGLINES: overlay.cpp:59 ('Throughput (active Logistic Points)') and the on-canvas legend title at body_surface_canvas.cpp:1490, which also prints 'anchor: N LP/tick' and 'N anchors - N LP/tick total'. PER-TILE NUMBERS: none today - the wash is the REACH-COST field (1 - sqrt(rc/p90)), not LP at all, and the only LP-valued mark is an anchor ring whose share is always exactly 1.0 because the legacy rate is uniform. LENSES.md:1020-1030 argues per-tile LP cannot vary for that reason; BL-1309 overtook that argument and nobody revisited it, since lp_coverage_at (logistic_points.cpp:342) is already a per-tile function and resolve_logistic_points already yields per-building coverage and grant fractions. Note the lens currently suppresses the hover card body-wide (:6058) as 'a value field with no structure grain' - that premise also goes once the field carries real per-tile numbers. PLAYER-FACING: no owner or nation filter exists anywhere in the path - collect_anchor_tile_set and body_reach_field are both body-wide. Filter to the player's home nation, and reconsider the suppressed border band (:3978) once it is one nation's network. ROADS, AND THE RENDERING ANSWER: the second road pass Ben noticed is real and deliberate - route_drawn goes true under this lens alone (:4216-4217), redrawing the network as vector curves over the baked road paint. Recolouring is CHEAP there: change the three IM_COL32 literals at :4224-4226 (track/road/highway) to the brighter white and leave the bake alone. The static-stroke cache key already includes overlay (:4484), so a lens toggle rebuilds strokes, never pixels. Do NOT try to brighten the BAKED asphalt per lens: bake_params carries no lens field and region_hash keys only tile fields, so adding one would re-bake every visible chunk on every lens toggle. Re-run tools/verify/throughput_field_census.cpp (LENSES.md:1043 requires it whenever the anchor set moves) and scripts/verify/throughput_lens.lua.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
items.title: A tile requests the points it needs and they are routed to it over one path, split across sources in distance order
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16, on the LP form: "Both: surfaces now, routing straight after"). DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section How a tile's points get to it. SEQUENCE IS BEN'S: BL-1352 (one system), BL-1353 (lens) and BL-1354 (tile surface) land FIRST, so routing is measured against honest numbers rather than guessed - the real model's reach already fades with distance and extends with outlying hubs, and nobody has yet seen it drawn. THE MODEL: today there is no routing at all - a nation-wide scalar pool scaled by a per-tile reach field (max over the nation's three networks), granted pro-rata or by the share rule. New: a tile's request is the sum of its buildings' needs; it is filled over ONE best path, never two at once; a source fills part of a request only if it both reaches the tile AND is itself connected back toward the market centre (Ben: "further sources have to both reach the tile, and produce enough to extend backward towards the market centre"), so points arrive along a chain the centre anchors and an isolated hub supplies nothing; where the nearest source falls short the remainder comes from the next nearest that satisfies both tests, in distance order. This supersedes the older constraint-2 rule that a draw lands on exactly one anchor. SCARCITY (Ben's ruling): distance ORDERS the queue and never raises the bill - requests inside the falloff range are served first, then those beyond, and a far building draws the same points as a near one. The settled rule 'the draw is what moves, not how far' therefore stands; NR-620 measured a 73% convoy-traffic collapse the one time a distance draw was tried, so any implementation that makes a far building cost more points is wrong by ruling, not by taste. MARCHES (Ben's ruling): a march draws the nation pool and competes with production. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): the march CLAIMS FIRST, keeping his 2026-09-24 ruling (NR-917) literally now that its other half is gone - it arbitrated armies against trade, and trade draws nothing, so a march is supplied before the production behind it. Written into LOGISTICS.md. Determinism: allocation must stay order-independent - a deterministic priority over a sorted set, never first-come by iteration order (the march draw is first-come in unit-id order today, economy_system.cpp:4210). A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability, haulage_measure --far-trade and per-nation output before and after.

items.title: A better road carries points further: Track 6, Road 8, Highway 10, fading to zero at double; rail carries 20 and delivers only where it connects
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): 'let's add an extension bonus to higher tiered roads. So tracks reach 6 tiles, roads reach 8, and highways reach 10 tiles. Railways can reach 20 tiles, but they only supply the exact tile they connect to.' RULED: those are FULL-STRENGTH distances and the fade runs to ZERO AT DOUBLE them (Ben, 2026-10-16) - track 6/12, road 8/16, highway 10/20. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section One pool. THE ROAD HALF IS A RECALIBRATION, not new mechanism: lp_full_reach[road] is 6 with per-tier step costs lp_road_step {_, 1.0, 0.7, 0.5}, which already yields 6 / 8.6 / 12 tiles - set the steps to 1.0 / 0.75 / 0.6 for 6 / 8 / 10, and lp_fade_length[road] = lp_full_reach[road] for the double-distance fade. THE RAIL HALF IS NEW BEHAVIOUR: lp_full_reach[rail] 10 -> 20, and delivery becomes point-to-point - the station's points land on the tile the line connects to and on no tile the line merely passes, which is the rule goods already obey (board and leave only at stations, section 4c). Sea is untouched and keeps 12 full / 8 fade; say so rather than quietly generalising the double-fade to it. items.author: Claude (from the BL-1351 census, 2026-10-17)
items.title: No doc owns where generation puts logistics sources, and what it puts there is not the picture Ben described
items.design: SPRINT 55 (from the BL-1351 census, 2026-10-17). Ben, 2026-10-16: 'What we want to see is a centralised market capital city, with a high number of logistics points, and logistics diminishing as we get further away, but extended by logistics buildings further away.' The census measured the opposite shape: 10.3% of hubs at market centres, points fading 83/73/65/39 across distance rings with the capital the peak in only 19% of cases and empty in 28%, and 78% of national ground at coverage 0 while every consumer is fully covered. The pass is honest - it walks CONSUMERS and covers each with one hub - so this is not a defect in it; it is that nothing ever asked it for a hierarchy. THE GAP THAT BLOCKS THE WORK: LOGISTICS.md section Logistic Points defines what a source IS and how reach fades, and says NOTHING about where the fold should put one, so Ben's picture has no owning doc and findings above have nothing to be pass/fail against. SO: Ben rules whether the centralised picture is the intent; it is written into LOGISTICS.md (or a generation doc) as the layout the fold owes; then the seeding pass is changed to seed hierarchically - centres and the capital first, outward after - and the census is re-run against it as pass/fail rather than as description. Sequenced after the road-tier reach extension (BL-1360) and rail point-to-point, both of which move these numbers. BEN RULED 2026-10-18: YES, the centralised-capital picture is the intent, and LOGISTICS.md owns it. Written that day as LOGISTICS.md section 'Where generation puts the sources - the capital is the peak': generation seeds hierarchically (strongest source at the capital, lesser ones at the other market centres, the periphery left for a player or rival to cover), and three rules become checks - every capital holds a source, no tile of a nation outruns its capital at generation, and uncovered GROUND is intended while CONSUMERS must be covered. How many sources and at what tier is in-band calibration, logged and re-measured by the coverage census rather than fixed in the doc. THE WORK: make generation seed that way and turn the BL-1351 census into a pass/fail gate on the three rules.

items.author: Claude (found verifying BL-1370/1371, 2026-10-17)
items.title: construction_ledger_tabs dies in staging: its fixture is refused for want of a road, not for want of funds
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found verifying BL-1370/1371 on main, 2026-10-17). scripts/verify/construction_ledger_tabs.lua exits 1 with ZERO assertions run - it dies in base.stage_ui_fixture (lib.lua:340, raised at :223) with 'fixture could not place a military base near the player's works: insufficient_funds'. The fixture runs up to 20 verify.econ_step(1) waiting out tech_locked and then places; the corp cannot pay by then. The delivering lane flagged it rather than claiming it pre-existing, which was right, and I could not attribute it either without a build at an older commit. CANDIDATES, in order: (1) BL-1335 taxes, merged the day before, now charge a share of operating profit every quarter the fixture steps - though the tax is floored at 0 so a loss-making fixture corp should pay nothing, which is the first thing to check; (2) the construction rate work changed what a build charges per tick; (3) market prices moved under the fixture so the base simply costs more. NOT a defect in the road or grid work: construction_progress (910), tile_card (71) and roads (31) all pass on the same build with zero failures. THE WORK: find which, then either fix the cause or fund the fixture honestly - never by widening the loop count, which would hide a real cost change. CORRECTED 2026-10-18, and MY FILED PREMISE WAS WRONG. The refusal is not affordability: once verify_api stopped collapsing refusals into 'failed' (see below), the message reads 'fixture could not place a military base near the player's works: needs_road' (lib.lua:249). It is the same BL-1347 gate, reached through place_near_player, which walks up to a 24-ring and is refused needs_road on every tile - so the three candidates I listed (taxes, construction rate, market prices) were all wrong, and the insufficient_funds text I quoted came from the collapsed enum, not from the treasury. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS A REAL DECISION, not a one-liner: roading every candidate before trying it would stamp about 2400 crossings, so the honest form is road-on-demand - try build_at, and only on needs_road road THAT tile and retry - which is correct ONLY IF needs_road is the LAST refusal can_place_in_world returns (otherwise a tile refused for the stack or the ceiling gets a road it never needed). Check that ordering first. It reaches about 20 scripts through stage_ui_fixture, so measure what roading each fixture switches on (reach discounts, and in one case the power-wire path) rather than assuming the placement is the only effect. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-18): CHECK THE ORDERING FIRST, then road-on-demand. Confirm needs_road is the LAST refusal can_place_in_world returns before building the retry, so a tile refused for a full stack or a full province ceiling never gets a road it did not need; if the ordering does not hold, fix the ordering or pick a different shape, and say which. Then road only the tile that was actually refused, never the whole candidate ring (about 2400 crossings). verify.stage_road exists for this and Ben granted its report of whether the write landed the same day.

items.design: SPRINT 55 (found delivering BL-1347, 2026-10-18). The delivering lane tried it and its run stalled in roads.lua's first wide capture past 5 GB; it then reproduced the SAME stall twice with the call removed, on a machine that had just run two 16-shard sweeps and where wc -l itself timed out, so the stall is UNATTRIBUTED and not evidence against the pass. items.author: Ben (2026-10-18, at the live click); filed by Claude
items.title: Where no neighbour admits a crossing, the road press should be muted and unpressable, with its explainer saying why
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-18, at the live click on BL-1347/1348/1357): 'When there are no legal road presses on a tile, we should mute the build button and stop it from being pressable, with a tooltip explaining it.' A DIRECT REVERSAL of the judgement BL-1370's lane took and the main session endorsed: it built the press disabled, decided that put the refusal back in the row, and left it live so the tile would arm and highlight nothing. Ben overruled it, and his reason is the better one - a press that arms and then does nothing teaches the player nothing about WHY, where a dead control that explains itself does. THE WORK: where road_crossing_targets returns an empty set, mute the press (BeginDisabled, as the unaffordable case already does) and put the reason on its per-column explainer - the explainer is the only place the reason lives, it does not come back as a row of red text. Note the affordability case already mutes, so the two must read differently: one says you cannot pay, the other that there is nowhere to go. Cover the rail track row too, which shares the grid. Update the ACTIONS.json entries for the press, and extend scripts/verify/roads.lua - it already asserts a zero-target tile arms and lights nothing, which is now the wrong assertion and must become: the press is disabled and its explainer names the reason. LIVE CLICK TAKEN (Ben, 2026-10-18): the muted road press behaves - dead rather than silent. Closed on his word. items.author: Claude (found by the BL-1380 lane, 2026-10-18)
items.title: The verify summary calls every failure a golden diff, which has now sent two readers to the wrong conclusion
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found by the BL-1380 lane, 2026-10-18). verify_api.cpp:7088 prints 'verify: %d capture(s) failed golden diff, %d script error(s)' from m_verify_failures - a counter that totals verify.expect failures AND golden diffs together. So a run with 13 failed assertions and no image diff at all reports '13 capture(s) failed golden diff'. CONSEQUENCE, twice over in one day: the delivering lane started from a false premise, and so did I - BL-1380 was filed saying 13 capture goldens diffed and would need Ben's ruling on a re-bless, when construction_progress.lua has NO goldens whatsoever (all 28 of its captures log 'no golden ... (capture-only)'). A re-bless is the most authorisation-sensitive act in this project (goldens are contracts, re-blessed only with Ben's go), so a line that invents one out of a failed assertion is worse than merely imprecise. THE WORK: say what is true - count assertion failures and golden diffs separately and name them separately, e.g. 'N assertion failure(s), M golden diff(s), K script error(s)'. One line, and it stops a class of wrong triage. DELIVERED 2026-10-18: m_verify_golden_failures counts the image diffs alone (app_capture.cpp's two sites), and both the per-script line and the run summary now name the two kinds apart - 'N failure(s): G golden diff(s), A assertion(s)'. PROVEN: roads.lua reads '0 failure(s): 0 golden diff(s), 0 assertion(s)' exit 0, and a two-failing-expect script reads '2 failure(s) - 0 capture(s) failed golden diff, 2 assertion(s) failed' exit 1.

items.author: Ben (live click on BL-1379, 2026-10-18)
items.title: A newly built road reads as connected in every direction, though the build is pairwise
items.design: SPRINT 55. BEN, in play on 2026-10-18: "It looks like roads are still rendered as adjoining even if the build is pairwise. When I build a new road tile, I see it connect in all possible directions, not just the direction it was built in." WHAT THE CODE SAYS, read the same day: the simulation is right - construction.cpp's lay_road_edge raises ONE crossing (both halves of that one edge), and BOTH draw paths gate on the edge mask, not on the neighbour: body_surface_canvas's draw_network skips a direction where road_tier_on_side is 0 ('nothing is laid across THIS boundary'), and the bake's road_links_of does the same before tile_pieces. So the all-directions read is NOT the two paths disagreeing with the mask, and three candidate causes remain, in order of likelihood: (1) the ARMED HIGHLIGHT persists after the lay, so the legal crossings still drawn around the new tile read as built road (BL-1370's highlight, drawn by the same press); (2) the NEIGHBOUR already carried generated edges on its other sides, so the junction genuinely connects several ways and only the new edge is new; (3) a stale bake chunk re-derived from road rather than road_sides. THE WORK: reproduce live at the zoom Ben was at, name which of the three it is, and fix that one - it is a visual triage item, so the live look comes before any code. It matters beyond itself because BL-1353's lens honesty rests on the road picture being true.

items.author: Claude (found running the gates for BL-1352, 2026-10-18)
items.title: lp_pool_harness's L7 old-version row has been red since roads became edges
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found running BL-1352's gates, 2026-10-18; NOT caused by it - that change touches no serialisation and save_roundtrip is green). lp_pool_harness reads 18 pass, 1 fail: 'L7 a v49 stream reads, every nation on the mechanical default'. CAUSE, read in the code rather than guessed: the row FABRICATES an old stream by writing a CURRENT snapshot, truncating the trailing share/space/tax sections, and overwriting the version word with k_world_save_version_pre_lp (49). That worked while the tile RECORD was version-independent. BL-1340 (v53) made it version-dependent - r_tile_v reads a u16 road_edges at the current version and a u8 legacy road_level below it - so a v53 body of bytes labelled v49 desyncs at the first tile and the reader refuses the whole stream. The assertion is therefore failing for a true reason: that stream is not a v49 stream. THE FIX is to produce a REAL old stream the way BL-1340 already does for its own case - world_save.cpp has write_world_snapshot_pre_road_edges / write_world_snapshot_at for exactly this - rather than relabelling bytes, and NOT to relax the row. Worth doing because the row guards a real migration (a pre-LP save must load with every nation on the mechanical share default) and a red row nobody owns is how a gate set rots.

items.author: Ben (in play, 2026-10-18)
items.title: The muted road press blamed the tier when the real refusal was another nation's ground
items.design: SPRINT 55. BEN, in play 2026-10-18: "I can't seem to find anywhere that's valid to build a road. Every tile with a road I try to press has the build button greyed out with 'nowhere left to cross from this tile at this tier'." MEASURED the same day by the new tools/verify/road_offer_census.cpp, which asks the rules the same question the UI asks, as the player's own corp, over the shipped seed-0 start: of 5017 ROADED tiles on the body only 53 (1.1%) admit a crossing, and 4647 of the refusals are FOREIGN GROUND (BL-1357), not the tier. On the player's OWN nation's ground 53 of 57 roaded tiles admit (93%) - but that nation holds 120 tiles of 31581, so 99.6% of what Ben can press is somebody else's country. THE RULE WORKED; THE SENTENCE LIED, and it lied in the way BL-1381 just made a rule about: it asserted a cause ('every side is either already roaded to this standard or one no crossing may take') that nothing had checked. DELIVERED 2026-10-18: ui::road_crossing_refusal asks can_place_road side by side and RANKS the answers - foreign ground first (no money or tier opens it), then nothing-here-to-build-from, then already-at-tier, then no-crossable-side - and the press's explainer says which one, so foreign ground now reads 'Another nation holds this tile. A road may cross INTO their ground, but never be built out of it - so build from your own side of the border.' WHAT IS STILL BEN'S: whether a corporation building only inside its home nation (plus one crossing over the border) is the intended reach, given that reach is 0.4% of the body. The census is the instrument for that call and prints the number for any seed. BEN RULED 2026-10-18: keep the home-nation-only reach; the new wording is enough. Written into LOGISTICS.md beside the border rule.
